data.name: Leviah
data.gender_notes: Leviah is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Hebrew, meaning ‘joined to Yahweh’, which is the name of the God of Israel in the Old Testament. In the Bible, Levites were the priests and gatekeepers of the tabernacle and temple, and they were responsible for carrying the ark of the covenant. The name Leviah carries the meaning “Joined to Yahweh” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Leviah usually hope their child will grow to embody joined to yahweh and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Close to God or a divine being
data.etymology: Leviah belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Joined to Yahweh.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Leviah total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

in_hebrew.long_meaning: לוויה הוא שם עברי שפירושו 'היא המשפיעה או מלווה את אלוהים'. השם לוויה נגזר מהמילה 'לוו', שפירושו 'ללוות' או 'להשפיע'. הוא שם שמשויך לנשיות ומראה על קשר הדוק עם האלוקים. השם מופיע ברשימות השמות הנוראים ביהדות ומראה על חשיבותה של הנושאת אותו.

in_greek.name: Λεβία
in_greek.meaning: Εκείνη που ενώνει ή συνοδεύει τον Θεό
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Λεβία είναι η ελληνική μορφή του εβραϊκού ονόματος לוויה, που σημαίνει 'Εκείνη που ενώνει ή συνοδεύει τον Θεό'. Στην ελληνική παράδοση, το όνομα Λεβία θεωρείται σύμβολο πνευματικής σύνδεσης και αφοσίωσης στον Θεό. Η ετυμολογία του ονόματος συνδέεται με την ιδέα της συντροφιάς και της πνευματικής εγγύτητας με το Θείο.

data.spiritual_symbolism: Leviah, meaning "joined to God" in Hebrew, symbolizes the deep connection and devotion of an individual to their divine savior. This name embodies a strong spiritual bond and unwavering faith.

historical_references.reference: In the Old Testament, Levi was the third son of Jacob and Leah. The tribe of Levi was the only tribe not allotted land in Canaan since they were the priests and gatekeepers of the tabernacle and later the temple. However, there is a mention of a person named Levi ben Sisera during the time of the Judges, who is considered a hero for killing the Canaanite warlord Sisera in retaliation for his brutal treatment of the Israelites.

In the New Testament, Levi is mentioned as a tax collector and one of the twelve apostles of Jesus Christ. He is often referred to as Matthew, as his gospel bears his name. Levi left his occupation as a tax collector to follow Jesus, signified by the symbol of a fish (Ichthus) which was a common symbol for Jesus and his disciples.

On Medium, writers with this name may publish articles on mindfulness practices, self-care, and spiritual awakening.
